Logistic Regression with Multiply-Imputed SCF Data

Source: R/scf_logit.R
scf_logit.Rd

Fits a logistic regression model using Rubin's Rules across all five implicates of a multiply-imputed SCF svrepdesign object. Supports reporting on the log-odds or odds-ratio scale.

scf_logit(design, formula, odds = FALSE)

Arguments

design

A multiply-imputed svrepdesign object created by scf_load().

formula

A model formula, e.g., ~ binary_outcome ~ predictors.

odds

Logical. If TRUE, exponentiates coefficients to return odds ratios. Default is FALSE (returns log-odds).

Value

A data.frame with:

  • term: model term

  • estimate: pooled coefficient (log-odds or odds ratio)

  • std.error: standard error

  • z.value: z-statistic

  • p.value: p-value

  • stars: conventional significance stars

Additional attributes:

  • "AIC": mean AIC across implicates

  • "models": list of glm models (1 per implicate)

Details

Internally, this function:

  • Fits glm(family = binomial()) on each implicate's data

  • Pools results using mitools::MIcombine()

  • Optionally exponentiates the final coefficients

The input data must be multiply-imputed and created via scf_load().

See also

scf_ols(), scf_glm(), scf_update(), scf_MIcombine()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Create binary outcome
scf2022 <- scf_update(scf2022, rich = networth > 1000000)

# Estimate model and print odds ratios
result <- scf_logit(scf2022, rich ~ age + factor(edcl), odds = TRUE)
knitr::kable(result, digits = 3)
} # }
